game: Mega Man Battle Network 6: Cybeast Gregar (USA)
about: Addresses, names and descriptions only: facts about the ROM, read from Cyberworld Endless's own sources (src/emu/*.h, src/core/rom.c, docs/ROM_DATA.md). No graphics, text, sound or code of the game. See docs/SYMBOLS.md.

14.title: Chip records (0x2C bytes)
14.how: Verify by listing the records whose words at 0x24 and 0x28 are equal: 34, all left out by the other rules but 275-277.

15.title: Chip names
15.how: Text archives found by encoding "Cannon" with the game's character table; pointers in code reference both.

16.title: Chip descriptions
16.how: Verify: script 1 of the first reads "Cannon to / attack / 1 enemy", script 0 of the second "Attk ahd. / Suck in & / shoot out" as in the disassembly.

19.title: Title screen
19.how: Check by drawing indices 1-0x4F of the picture with that cut: no 6 pixels remain and the N keeps its outline.

20.title: Title marks
20.how: Check with `build.py shot --scene title --marks 1FE`: each mark whole, in its colours, where BN6 puts it.

21.title: Boot and warps
21.how: Found in the bn6f disassembly and tested in `tools/romlab`.

22.title: The game's structures read field by field
22.how: Verified by `CYBERWORLD_STATE_POS=1`, whose state prints MegaMan's position and every NPC's (`npc N ... at x y z`) where they stand on the map, and by an autopilot run whose log is the same, line for line, as before the names.

23.title: Encounter roll
23.how: Verify with an autopilot run: its random and guardian battles, and its log, as before.

24.title: Battle events by hook
24.how: Verify: an autopilot run's log is the same as before.

25.title: Map, flag and key item events by hook
25.how: Verify: an autopilot run's log is the same as before; a layer's challenge and its Undernet warp start on a Yes (`tools/play.py start ch --fresh --seed 31 -- --scene emu --run-depth 4 --dev quiet --talk challenge:300`; `--seed 41`, `--run-depth 4 --net-biome 4 --talk undernet:300`); a ScrtData picked up is counted and MegaMan says what it is for (`--seed 53`, `--run-depth 5`: its Mystery Data at 348, -44, MegaMan put beside it with the dev step `place 328 -44 0`); a guardian's exit pad stays shut after each battle on its layer and after a CONTINUE there.

26.title: BN6's wait for a frame
26.how: Verify: the autopilot's debug log and run log are the same with and without it, and `CYBERWORLD_EMU_DEBUG`'s 30-frame line counts about four more hook hits a frame (each interrupt that wakes the CPU before VBlank brings it back to the loop).

29.title: Purple Mystery Data and the Unlocker
29.how: Verify: a seed whose layer holds one (`CYBERWORLD_STATE_POS=map` marks it L), A on it says it is locked; with `--talk keys:FRAME` (an Unlocker by GiveItem) it asks, and Yes gives the chip.

30.title: Rush's gaps
30.how: Verified: live in romlab on Central Area 2 and with its gap moved to comp map 0x8C:0 through the repointed literals; on a generated layer (seed 8, depth 2) A with RushFood ran the cutscene, Rush lay in the gap, MegaMan crossed both ways and took the island's data; without RushFood the edge held.

31.title: Teleports and the pads' centrepieces
31.how: Verify: seed 12 at depth 2 in Green Area (`--net-biome 3`): stepping on the gem by the way beams MegaMan to the island's gem and back.

32.title: Link Navi obstacles and security cubes
32.how: Verify: seed 6 at depth 2 in a comp (`--net-biome 8`): A at the cube names it and asks around, the teller eight panels on tells its code, then A at the cube enters it and it vanishes; seed 4 at depth 2 in Seaside (`--net-biome 1 --talk zenny:300`): the toll takes 200 of 10000 zenny, and with none MegaMan says so.

35.title: Chip Traders
35.how: Verify by dumping a pool's first records beside the chips' own codes at `chip_data` (the same bytes), by `CYBERWORLD_EMU_DEBUG`'s "trader: N of M chips" line (74 of 108 for the Standard folder at a depth-8 trader), and by trading at a layer's trader (there: Roll *, TrnArrw1 A, M-Cannon S).

36.title: The BugFrag Trader's trade
36.how: Verify with `tools/play.py start bt --seed 11835737 -- --scene emu --net-biome 4 --run-depth 2 --talk bugfrags:2600,bugtrader:2800`, A pressed through Chaud's call first: Yes gives a Navi chip (ChrgeMan \*, in the pack), 50 BugFrags become 40 (the state's `bugfrags`), five trades end at 0 and the sixth Yes shows the not-enough line and ends the chat, no chip given; after No at either question the chat ends and the PET opens.

38.title: Shops
38.how: Verify: decompress the text with and without the byte changed: exactly seven bytes differ, each a face; a program shop's window then shows the face its chat does.

43.title: The Library
43.how: Found from that routine; checked by listing the set flags at a new run's first layer (exactly the Standard folder's twelve chips: 1, 4, 5, 54, 71, 72, 89, 154, 163, 175, 184, 192, which the boot's NEW GAME gave), and by setting a profile's chips at a run's start and reading the PET's LIBRARY (StdChip 15/200, the Blade folder's LongSwrd, PanlGrab and Barrier among them).

46.title: Warp pads
46.how: Checked by placing MegaMan in the left corner cell of a layer's exit pad: he warps.

48.title: Net maps
48.how: Checked by drawing each layer alone (`area_src_render` with the other layer cleared) and both as the game shows them; `tiles.c` learns a tile's first layer alone where it draws the floor, and its second too only where the floor needs it.

55.title: BN6's own DarkChips: DrkSword, DarkThnd, DrkRecov, DarkInvs, DarkPlus
55.how: Verify, as seen headless with a throwaway hook (not committed) that wrote the folder in code * and marked it owned as own_folder_chips does, set the BugFrags through GiveBugfrags or TakeBugfrags and raised the battle's enemies to 2000 HP (`--seed 13`, its first battle a Mettaur): with 5 BugFrags DrkSword dealt 400 in a magenta crescent (a Mettaur two columns ahead and a row down deleted, a Starfish three columns ahead untouched), the BugFrags 5 to 4 at the use, save and battle's copy alike, the HP bug 2; DarkThnd 200, a purple Thunder ball, the Mettaur paralysed, the HP bug 1; DrkRecov 50 to 1050 of 2000 HP, the HP bug 7, then 1 HP each 10 frames; DarkInvs a time freeze named DarkInvs, then 480 frames of MegaMan as a green phantom slashing and firing his held Cannon on his own, LEFT held for 200 frames not keeping him in the back column, untouched by the Mettaur's shockwaves; DarkPlus after a Cannon left the HUD at "Cannon 40" with two chip icons and dealt 40 (Atk+10 in its place: "Cannon 40+10"), and alone made a puff, took a BugFrag and gave the HP bug 4.

56.title: BN6's own DarkChips in a run

57.title: The run's buster in BN5's battles
57.how: Verify in the game: an Attack+1 run (seed 6's layer-1 gift with `--run-depth 1 --net-biome x0`, placed and RUN in the NaviCust, STATUS then showing Attack LV 2) prints "guest: battle ..., buster Attack 2, Speed 1, Charge 1" and "guest: its battle's buster Attack 2, Speed 1, Charge 1" with `CYBERWORLD_EMU_DEBUG=1`, and its first shot takes a Mettaur from 40 HP to 38.

61.title: GiveZenny
61.how: Verify: a guest battle won on a BN5 layer adds its results screen's zenny to the PET's.

62.title: Sprites behind the second layer
62.how: Found by logging OAM entries near the screen's middle and the object's bytes per area (`--net-biome 0`-`17`); check: +0xA5 reads 0x0C on a layer in 0x91:0 and 0x08 in 0x91:1.

63.title: Real-world maps
63.how: Checked by drawing all 37 maps (`build.py world`) and comparing the game's VRAM and palette RAM on Central Town with the decoded tile set: tiles 0-819 match, colours 0-207 match.

64.title: Real-world map takeover
64.how: Found beside their internet counterparts in bn6f `asm03_1_0.s` and `asm03_0.s` (the real-world tables come first, 7 entries each); each pointer read from the Gregar ROM leads to its group's code or lists.

68.title: Checks
68.how: Found in Gregar as the literal (pool word `0x08040790`) of the second of three look-alike routines (`0x08040768`, bn6f `chatbox_selectCompTextByMap_8040794`); Central Town's table `0x0804F800` gives scripts 0-4, none, 6-10, 12, 13 for checks 0-12, ACDC Town's 0-7.

69.title: Jack-in
69.how: The table was found in Gregar by its first records (Falzar `0x080984C8`).

76.title: Props' map objects
76.how: Found in each map's object list (the group's spawner's first `ldr r1, [pc, #imm]` literal) and checked by spawning each in a generated layer and in its own place.

77.title: The NaviCust's Spins
77.how: CheckKeyItem (bn6f `0x0803CE2C`) answers 0 for an item whose check byte (`+0x78` array) differs from its seed (`0x020004E0` array) XOR `0x55`: Gregar's code at `0x006E3C` writes the check as the game gives an item, `0x006E50` tests it (Falzar's key is `0x6F`).

79.title: Net maps' backdrops and animations
79.how: Verify: in romlab, warped into each BN5 map, its BG palette (`0x05000000`, dumped every 32 frames) changes in those banks and no others; with BN5 beside BN6, `CYBERWORLD_EMU_DEBUG=1` prints "xbackdrop: ... map 0x90:0's backdrop and animations for 0x90:0" (0x93:0 for 0x91:1, 0x94:3 for 0x92:0), a capture of `--net-biome x0`, `x2` or `x3` over a few hundred frames shows BN5's backdrop moving and the GFXAnim slots at `0x020094C0` naming the copies, and BN6's own areas (`--seed 11` dresses none) draw frame for frame as without BN5.

80.title: Battle backgrounds
80.how: Verify: with BN5 beside BN6, `CYBERWORLD_EMU_DEBUG=1` prints "xbackdrop: background 8 ... as 0x16" (10, 15 and 25 as 0x17-0x19), and a battle on `--net-biome x0` to `x3` (`--seed 2`, the autopilot finds one) shows BN5's background: ACDC Area's blue diamonds, SciLab's scrolling binary, End Area's red field of diamonds, Nebula Area's still stars.

81.title: The PET menu
81.how: Verify: in a run, the PET shows Save lit and Comm grey; A on Comm buzzes, A on Save closes the PET and "Run saved" shows.

82.title: The PET's KeyItem and E-Mail words
82.how: Verify: in a run, KeyItem lists NaviCode and LibCard with their words, and E-Mail a mail from Dad per guardian met, its body the guardian's warning.

83.title: Field objects and the in-battle Mystery Data
83.how: Verify: `--dev gem` puts one in every random battle; win without touching it and the results give a second reward (980 zenny on layer 3), hit it and it breaks.

84.title: Enemy stats
84.how: Checked: Mettaur 40/80/120/160 HP, 10/20/40/60 damage; BlastMan 400/800/1400; Colonel (navi ai 18) 1200/1600/2000.

85.title: Enemy traits
85.how: Checked: navi ais 3 SlashMan 0x80/0x10 (Sword, weak to Breaker), 4 EraseMan 0x40/0x20 (Cursor, Wind), 8 TenguMan 0x20/0x80 (Wind, Sword), 9 GroundMan and 10 DustMan 0x10/0x40 (Breaker, Cursor), every other guardian 0/0, as the Rockman EXE Zone wiki's BN6 boss list has them; virus families 25 DarkMech 0/0x40 and 26 SnakeArm 0/0x20, the rest of the run's 0/0.

90.title: Battle rewards
90.how: Found in romlab from the results screen's reward back to the chooser; verify: two Mettaurs at Busting S give Rflectr1 A, and with their row's chip entries recoded to P in the core's copy, the results screen and the pack show Rflectr1 P.

91.title: The battle's DeleteTime
91.how: Verify: win a battle and compare its frames / 60 with the DeleteTime the results screen shows.

92.title: Chips owned
92.how: Found from GiveFolder's per-chip step (`sub_8021B2A`); verify: a folder of LongSwrd, Barrier and PanlGrab written into RAM plays blank in every hand, and with their marks set they draw and play.

93.title: Running from a battle
93.how: Found in romlab on a story BlastMan EX battle: its word (`0x189D7`) refuses, patched to `0x189F7` or `0x49E2` it asks; verify: a guardian's battle says "no time to run away".

94.title: Custom gauge
94.how: Verify: in battle it climbs from 0 to 0x4000 in about 512 frames and drops to 0 as the Custom screen opens.

95.title: The autopilot's fight
95.how: Verify: `CYBERWORLD_AUTOPILOT=1 python3 build.py shot --scene emu --seed 3 --frames 15000` wins seed 3's depth-2 Piranhas at 100 HP (`runlog.txt`), where the button rhythm the autopilot had used, still `weak`'s, picked an Atk+10 alone and was deleted.

96.title: Chat font
96.how: Verify: code 0x0F is an `E` whose top row reads `0x11`, and its width byte is 8.

99.title: Mugshots
99.how: Verified by the decoded sheet and by counting `F5 00 id` in the Gregar text archives.

102.title: NaviCust
102.how: Checked against the NaviCust screen: SuprArmr and Custom1 cannot share the 4x4 board without a bug (a playtester's, and `navicust_pack`), and share the 5x4.

103.title: The Custom screen's window
103.how: Verify: the same, in any battle.

104.title: NaviCust compression
104.how: Verify: with Custom1 in the PET, `play.py` dev step `flags 9832 9835 1` (0x2668-0x266B; the step reaches every flag of eEventFlags' 1448 bytes, `BN6_EVENT_FLAG_BYTES`, bn6f's ewram.s) draws it in its four-block shape on the NaviCust screen; with it placed and SuperArmor's flags 0x2664-0x2667 set too, MegaMan says SuperArmor needs a program moved, where uncompressed it would not fit the 4x4 board at all.

105.title: Program Advances
105.how: Verify: the first entry is `03 04 53 01 47 00 48 00 49 00` (LifeSrd from 71, 72, 73), the fourteenth `03 00 40 01 01 00` (GigaCan1 from three Cannons in a row), the forty-fourth `03 04 40 01 01 00 01 00 0C 00` (GigaCan1 from Cannon, Cannon, TankCan1: the Gate's).

106.title: The All * helper
106.how: Verify: with All *, three Cannon * staged as a first hand's first picks show "PrgAdvance" and GigaCan1 (with `0x2A01` left there, three Cannons fire one by one); the gift's TimeBom2 (codes C D E) reads TimeBom2 * in the PET's pack, and a folder's Sword moved to the pack and back reads Sword * there and in the folder.

107.title: NaviCust compression codes
107.how: Verify: Custom1's row spells L B B R B A A L R R; held RIGHT on Custom1 in the NaviCust's list, those ten buttons draw its four-block shape.

108.title: Reg memory and RegUps
108.how: Verify: dev talk `regup` (RegUP3) on a fresh run: MegaMan says 7 MB, and the folder shows 7MB.

110.title: NaviCust's board
110.how: Check with `tools/romlab`: load a state with programs placed and dump both.

111.title: MP2K song table
111.how: Verify: the entries' headers, their first byte (tracks) 0.

113.title: Dev tools
113.how: Flag `0x173E`, tested next, is the SlipRun state: the player's update clears it every frame (bn6f `ow_player.s`), so setting it does nothing.
